correctness.rationale: For Wagner graph W=M8 with cycle edges i,i+1 and four antipodal chords i,i+4, the Lipschitz-free ball is the symmetric edge polytope in the 7-dimensional zero-sum subspace. Polar potentials f mod constants satisfy |f(u)-f(v)|≤1 on 12 edges; a supporting polar vertex has a tight-edge signed incidence matrix of rank7 iff its tight subgraph connects and spans. Thus all polar vertices are integral mod constants by spanning-tree edge steps, and graph diameter2 bounds normalized potential values to {0,1,2}. The finite search over all 3^8 ternary words is mathematically exhaustive. A separately reconstructed checker enumerates 222 feasible connected-tight potential classes and splits them into 13 disjoint orbits under dihedral16 and f↦-f, with orbit sizes 2,4,8, seven 16s, and three 32s; exact totals 222, two-level58, three-level164 and tight-edge distribution 7:32,8:54,9:80,10:56. Independently fixing f(0)=0 and checking integer potentials from [-2,2] is an additional finite normalization check. General facet criterion is cited prior work, not asserted original.

value.rationale: The Wagner graph (eight-vertex Möbius ladder), a canonical nonplanar cubic metric graph, and its Lipschitz-free/symmetric edge polytope are natural objects. The complete dihedral-plus-antipodal facet orbit census, tight-edge spectrum and potential-height spectrum supply structurally nontrivial exact finite geometry data beyond generic facet generation. This precise full classification can support invariant metric/polytope comparisons and is not an arbitrary unlabeled subset or a bare known count; claims of a family theorem or all polytope automorphisms are explicitly excluded.
